sector_model: bank holding company (Indiana, Kentucky, Ohio); use earnings, tangible book, net interest margin, credit quality, capital ratios, funding; no FCF model; AOCI securities losses shown separately
thesis: German American is a 8.4B asset community bank that earned 38.6M in Q3 2026 (diluted EPS 1.03, +10%) and 145.6M over the TTM. At 50.08 (2026-11-06) it trades at about 12.9x TTM earnings, 1.63x book and 2.5x tangible book (20.01 per share), with a 2.5% dividend yield (1.24 annualized). Net interest margin rose to 4.42% in Q3 (tax equivalent) from 4.06%, efficiency ratio about 52%, annualized net charge-offs 4 bps, non-accrual loans fell to 23.7M (0.39% of loans) from 29.3M at year end, allowance 79.3M (1.32% of loans, 3.3x non-accrual), CET1 14.26% and total risk-based capital 15.74%.
counterthesis: Valuation is not cheap for a bank at 2.5x tangible book, and 17 bps of the 9M26 margin comes from accretion of acquired loan discounts that will fade. Roughly 3.27B (55%) of loans are commercial real estate, 13.2M special mention and 24.0M substandard in one commercial class, and CRE stress could lift losses. AOCI loss of 250.8M (21.7% of equity) reflects 1.59B of securities with unrealized losses that depress tangible equity; deposits fell 53M in 9M26 and FHLB and other borrowings rose to 268M from 183M, so funding is tightening. Loan growth is only 3% annualized. Prior-year EPS comparison is helped by 17.2M of 2025 provision tied to the Heartland acquisition (4.0M in 9M26) which flatters 9M earnings growth (+43%). 10-K, deposit mix by uninsured share and CRE segment detail were not read.
invalidation: Net interest margin falling below 3.9% as acquired-loan accretion ends; non-accrual loans above 1% of loans or net charge-offs above 25 bps; CET1 below 11%; deposit outflows forcing more wholesale funding; CRE special mention and substandard balances rising for two quarters; loan growth stalling.
